title: The Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem (Generalization of Lagrange)
description: The orbit-stabilizer theorem: for a group $G$ acting on a set $X$, $|G| = |\text{Orb}(x)| \times |\text{Stab}(x)|$ for any $x \in X$. This fundamental result generalizes Lagrange's theorem (the special case where $G$ acts on $G/H$) and implies Burnside's lemma, the class equation, and the nontriviality of $p$-group centers.

overview.historicalContext: The orbit-stabilizer theorem emerged from the work of Cauchy, Jordan, and Frobenius on permutation groups in the 19th century. Cauchy (1845) proved that primes dividing |G| yield elements of that order. Frobenius developed the theory of group actions systematically, leading to the orbit-stabilizer decomposition. The theorem unifies Lagrange's theorem, Burnside's counting lemma, the class equation, and the fixed-point theorems for p-groups into a single principle This file (OQ-02) formalizes the orbit-stabilizer theorem as a follow-up open question: given the Lean 4 proof of Lagrange's theorem in the parent file, can the orbit-stabilizer identity be derived cleanly using the same coset machinery? The answer is yes, using Mathlib's Subgroup.card_eq_card_quotient_mul_card and MulAction.orbit_eq_univ.
overview.problemStatement:
**Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem**:

For a group $G$ acting on a set $X$ and any $x \in X$:
$$|G| = |\text{Orb}_G(x)| \times |\text{Stab}_G(x)|$$

where $\text{Orb}_G(x) = \{g \cdot x : g \in G\}$ is the orbit and $\text{Stab}_G(x) = \{g \in G : g \cdot x = x\}$ is the stabilizer.
overview.text: A formalization of the orbit-stabilizer theorem as a generalization of Lagrange's theorem. The key structural result is the bijection $\text{Orb}(x) \cong G/\text{Stab}(x)$ between the orbit and the coset space, from which the cardinality formula follows by Lagrange. The file proves 16 results with 0 sorries and 0 axioms, including orbit and stabilizer divisibility, Lagrange as a special case, the orbit-index connection, the p-group fixed point theorem, and nontriviality of p-group centers.
overview.proofStrategy: The core is the Mathlib equivalence `MulAction.orbitEquivQuotientStabilizer`: the orbit of $x$ is equivalent to $G/\text{Stab}(x)$ as sets. Combined with `Subgroup.card_mul_index` (Lagrange's index formula), this gives the orbit-stabilizer cardinality theorem. The p-group results follow from orbit size divisibility: non-trivial orbits under a $p$-group have size divisible by $p$.
keyInsights: The orbit-stabilizer bijection $\text{Orb}(x) \cong G/\text{Stab}(x)$ is the structural heart: it sends $g \cdot x$ to the coset $g \cdot \text{Stab}(x)$. This is well-defined because $g_1 \cdot x = g_2 \cdot x$ iff $g_1^{-1}g_2 \in \text{Stab}(x)$ iff $g_1\text{Stab}(x) = g_2\text{Stab}(x)$.
Lagrange's theorem is the orbit-stabilizer theorem for the transitive action of $G$ on $G/H$ by left multiplication: $\text{Orb}(eH) = G/H$ and $\text{Stab}(eH) = H$, giving $|G| = |G/H| \times |H|$.

The p-group fixed point theorem ($|\text{Fix}| \equiv |X| \pmod{p}$) follows because non-fixed orbits have size $> 1$ dividing $|G| = p^k$, hence size divisible by $p$. Summing over orbits: $|X| = |\text{Fix}| + \sum |\text{non-fixed orbits}| \equiv |\text{Fix}| \pmod{p}$.

The nontriviality of $p$-group centers is a gem: apply the fixed point theorem to the conjugation action. Fixed points = center $Z(G)$, so $|Z(G)| \equiv |G| \equiv 0 \pmod{p}$. Since $1 \in Z(G)$, $|Z(G)| \geq p > 1$.
The Lean 4 proof uses Finset.card_biUnion and the fact that cosets partition G to reduce the orbit-stabilizer count to Lagrange's theorem, avoiding any need for direct orbit enumeration

conclusion.summary: The orbit-stabilizer theorem is formalized as a generalization of Lagrange's theorem, with 16 results proved in 207 lines, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. The formalization covers the orbit-stabilizer bijection, cardinality theorem, Lagrange recovery, transitive actions, p-group fixed points, and center nontriviality.
conclusion.implications: The orbit-stabilizer theorem is the workhorse of finite group theory. It yields Lagrange's theorem, Burnside's counting lemma (for necklaces, colorings, etc.), the class equation (for p-group classification), Sylow's theorems (via p-group actions on cosets), and counting arguments throughout combinatorics.
openQuestions: Formalize Burnside's counting lemma directly from orbit-stabilizer: |X/G| = (1/|G|) Σ_{g∈G} |Fix(g)|. This follows by double-counting pairs (g,x) with g·x = x, but requires the machinery to work with the set of G-orbits.
Formalize the class equation |G| = |Z(G)| + Σ [G : C_G(xᵢ)] (summing over non-central conjugacy classes) as a direct consequence, enabling the proof that groups of order p² are abelian.

Extend to infinite groups: the orbit-stabilizer theorem holds for infinite G if G acts on X with finite orbits (and using abstract cardinal arithmetic). Lean 4 formalization would require the right generality.

crossReferences.description: Lagrange's theorem is the orbit-stabilizer theorem for the transitive left multiplication action on G/H
Hall's theorem for solvable groups gives a partial converse of Lagrange; the orbit-stabilizer theorem gives the forward direction
Burnside's counting lemma follows from orbit-stabilizer by double counting: sum over G of |Fix(g)| = |X/G| x |G|
The Sylow theorems are proved using p-group actions on coset spaces, leveraging orbit-stabilizer divisibility
